meaning.en: Smug and self-satisfied.
meaning.zh: 形容自以为了不起而得意的样子。

examples.zh: 他取得一点成绩就洋洋自得。
examples.en: He gets smug over the smallest achievement.

examples.zh: 看他那洋洋自得的样子。
examples.en: Look how pleased with himself he is.

meaning.en: Rude and unreasonable; overbearing.
meaning.zh: 态度粗暴，不讲道理。

examples.zh: 这个顾客蛮横无理，大吵大闹。
examples.en: The customer was rude and unreasonable, kicking up a huge fuss.

examples.zh: 对蛮横无理的要求要坚决拒绝。
examples.en: Firmly refuse unreasonable demands.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. 横 is hèng here.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。"横"读 hèng。

natural: Meeting misfortune and turning it into luck

meaning.en: To turn bad luck into good.
meaning.zh: 遇到凶险，转化为吉利。

examples.zh: 他多次遇险，都能逢凶化吉。
examples.en: He's been in danger many times and always landed on his feet.

examples.zh: 愿您逢凶化吉，一切平安。
examples.en: May any misfortune turn to good luck, and may all be well.

natural: Red peach blossom and green willows

meaning.en: The bright colours of spring.
meaning.zh: 桃花嫣红，柳枝碧绿。形容春天美丽的景色。

examples.zh: 三月的江南桃红柳绿。
examples.en: Southern China in March is ablaze with peach blossom and green willows.

examples.zh: 湖边桃红柳绿，游人如织。
examples.en: The lakeside is bright with spring colour and full of visitors.

meaning.en: To try diplomacy first before resorting to force.
meaning.zh: 先按礼节同对方交涉，行不通时再用武力或其他强硬手段解决。

examples.zh: 我们先礼后兵，先和对方谈判。
examples.en: We'll try diplomacy first and negotiate with them.

examples.zh: 他先礼后兵，警告无效后才报了警。
examples.en: He tried the friendly approach first and only called the police when warnings failed.

natural: Chickens and dogs heard from one to the next

meaning.en: (Of villages) close together; a peaceful rural scene.
meaning.zh: 鸡鸣狗叫的声音彼此都能听到。形容住处相距很近。

examples.zh: 几个村子鸡犬相闻，来往方便。
examples.en: The villages are within earshot of each other and easy to travel between.

examples.zh: 邻居鸡犬相闻，却老死不相往来。
examples.en: The neighbours lived within earshot yet never visited each other.

story.en: Laozi's ideal small state: "Neighbouring states can see each other and hear each other's chickens and dogs, yet the people grow old and die without visiting." Tao Yuanming later used it for his Peach Blossom Spring.
story.zh: 《老子》："邻国相望，鸡犬之声相闻，民至老死不相往来。"陶渊明《桃花源记》也写"阡陌交通，鸡犬相闻"。

usage.en: Predicate. Often with 老死不相往来.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与"老死不相往来"连用。

meaning.en: Schemes and intrigues.
meaning.zh: 暗中策划的阴险毒辣的计谋。

examples.zh: 他的阴谋诡计终于被揭穿了。
examples.en: His schemes were finally exposed.

examples.zh: 宫廷里充满了阴谋诡计。
examples.en: The court was full of intrigue.

meaning.en: An open feint to cover a secret move.
meaning.zh: 公开地修复栈道，以迷惑对方。比喻用假象迷惑对方。

examples.zh: 明修栈道，暗度陈仓。
examples.en: Openly repair the plank roads, secretly march via Chencang.

examples.zh: 他明修栈道，表面上跟这家公司谈，暗地里另找了合作方。
examples.en: As a feint he negotiated openly with the firm while secretly finding another partner.

story.en: Han Xin had soldiers openly repair the burned plank roads, convincing the enemy he would come that way, while he secretly led the army via Chencang.
story.zh: 韩信派兵公开修复栈道迷惑敌人，暗中率军从陈仓小路出击。

usage.en: Usually in 明修栈道，暗度陈仓.
usage.zh: 常说"明修栈道，暗度陈仓"。

natural: Three in the morning, four in the evening

meaning.en: Fickle; constantly changing one's mind (especially in love).
meaning.zh: 原指以诈术欺人。后比喻常常变卦，反复无常。

examples.zh: 他感情上朝三暮四，让人不放心。
examples.en: He's so fickle in love that no one trusts him.

examples.zh: 做事不能朝三暮四。
examples.en: Don't keep chopping and changing.

story.en: A monkey-keeper offered his monkeys three nuts in the morning and four in the evening; they were furious. He offered four in the morning and three in the evening; they were delighted — though the total was the same.
story.zh: 养猴人给猴子分橡子，说早上三个晚上四个，猴子都发怒；改说早上四个晚上三个，猴子都高兴了。

usage.en: Predicate. 朝 is zhāo. Today means fickle, not the original sense of trickery.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。"朝"读 zhāo。现义为反复无常。

natural: Words forming an essay as they leave the mouth

meaning.en: Eloquent; speaking as well as one writes.
meaning.zh: 话说出来就成文章。形容文思敏捷，口才好。

examples.zh: 他学识渊博，出口成章。
examples.en: He's so learned that he speaks as eloquently as he writes.

examples.zh: 这位主持人出口成章，妙语连珠。
examples.en: The host is wonderfully eloquent and witty.

natural: Seven or eight out of ten

meaning.en: Nearly all; mostly done. Also: odds and ends.
meaning.zh: 表示接近完成或差不多。也指零零碎碎、杂七杂八。

examples.zh: 作业已经做得七七八八了。
examples.en: My homework is pretty much done.

examples.zh: 他把七七八八的东西都塞进了抽屉。
examples.en: He stuffed all his bits and bobs into the drawer.

usage.en: Complement or attributive. Colloquial, especially in southern Chinese speech.
usage.zh: 多作补语、定语，口语，南方常用。

meaning.en: To think oneself extraordinary; conceited.
meaning.zh: 自以为不平凡，比别人高明。

examples.zh: 他自命不凡，看不起同事。
examples.en: He thinks he's special and looks down on his colleagues.

examples.zh: 自命不凡的人往往难以合作。
examples.en: Conceited people are often hard to work with.

meaning.en: In rags; too poor to clothe oneself properly.
meaning.zh: 衣服破烂，遮不住身体。形容生活极端贫困。

examples.zh: 旧社会，穷人衣不蔽体，食不果腹。
examples.en: In the old society, the poor were in rags and went hungry.

examples.zh: 灾民们衣不蔽体，急需救援。
examples.en: The disaster victims are barely clothed and urgently need help.

usage.en: Predicate. Often with 食不果腹.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与"食不果腹"连用。

meaning.en: Good deeds are rewarded.
meaning.zh: 做好事会得到好的报答。

examples.zh: 善有善报，恶有恶报。
examples.en: Good is rewarded with good, and evil with evil.

examples.zh: 她一直帮助别人，善有善报，大家也都帮她。
examples.en: She always helps others, and what goes around comes around — everyone helps her too.

usage.en: Usually in 善有善报，恶有恶报.
usage.zh: 常说"善有善报，恶有恶报"。

meaning.en: Headstrong and self-opinionated; refusing advice.
meaning.zh: 倔强固执，自以为是，不考虑别人的意见。

examples.zh: 他刚愎自用，不听劝告，最终失败。
examples.en: He was headstrong, ignored advice and ultimately failed.

examples.zh: 领导者不能刚愎自用。
examples.en: A leader mustn't be self-opinionated.

story.en: Before the Battle of Bi, a Chu officer predicted Jin's defeat because its deputy commander Xian Hu was "stubborn and unkind, unwilling to take orders" (刚愎不仁).
story.zh: 《左传》："其佐先縠刚愎不仁，未肯用命。"

meaning.en: Take care of yourself; mind how you go (often a warning).
meaning.zh: 自己妥善处理。常用作劝诫或警告。

equivalents: don't say I didn't warn you

examples.zh: 我该说的都说了，你好自为之吧。
examples.en: I've said all I can — you're on your own now.

examples.zh: 这是最后一次机会，你好自为之。
examples.en: This is your last chance — watch your step.

usage.en: Standalone or predicate. Often a stern warning or farewell.
usage.zh: 多单独成句，常带警告意味。

natural: The carp leaping over the Dragon Gate

meaning.en: A sudden rise in status (especially by passing exams).
meaning.zh: 比喻中举、升官等飞黄腾达的事，也比喻逆流前进，奋发向上。

examples.zh: 他考上名牌大学，真是鲤鱼跳龙门。
examples.en: Getting into a top university was his big leap up the ladder.

examples.zh: 每个农村孩子都盼望鲤鱼跳龙门。
examples.en: Every rural child dreams of a rags-to-riches leap.

usage.en: Predicate or object. From the legend that a carp leaping the Dragon Gate falls on the Yellow River becomes a dragon.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、宾语。传说鲤鱼跃过黄河龙门就会化为龙。

meaning.en: Onlookers see more clearly than those involved.
meaning.zh: 旁观的人看得清楚。

equivalents: the onlooker sees most of the game
can't see the wood for the trees (for those involved)

examples.zh: 当局者迷，旁观者清。
examples.en: Those involved are confused; the onlooker sees clearly.

examples.zh: 你问问朋友的看法吧，旁观者清。
examples.en: Ask your friends — an outsider sees more clearly.

story.en: The scholar Yuan Xingchong wrote: "Those in the game are deluded; those watching from the side see clearly" (当局称迷，傍观见审).
story.zh: 《旧唐书·元行冲传》："当局称迷，傍观见审。"

natural: Holding great ambitions in one's heart

meaning.en: To harbour great ambitions.
meaning.zh: 心中怀有远大的志向。

examples.zh: 他从小就胸怀大志。
examples.en: He's had big dreams since childhood.

examples.zh: 年轻人要胸怀大志，脚踏实地。
examples.en: Young people should aim high but keep their feet on the ground.

natural: A frog at the bottom of a well

meaning.en: A person with a narrow outlook.
meaning.zh: 井底的青蛙只能看到井口那么大的一块天。比喻见识狭窄的人。

examples.zh: 多出去看看世界，别做井底之蛙。
examples.en: Get out and see the world — don't be a frog in a well.

examples.zh: 不了解行业动态，就会成为井底之蛙。
examples.en: Without following industry trends, you'll become parochial.

story.en: Zhuangzi: "You can't talk about the sea with a frog in a well — it is limited by its space." A frog boasts of its well to a turtle from the Eastern Sea, until the turtle describes the ocean.
story.zh: 《庄子·秋水》："井蛙不可以语于海者，拘于虚也。"井蛙向东海之鳖夸耀自己的井，鳖讲述大海之大。

pinyin: duō xíng bù yì bì zì bì
literal: much · do · not · righteous · surely · self · perish
natural: Do much evil and you will surely destroy yourself

meaning.en: Evildoers bring about their own downfall.
meaning.zh: 坏事做多了，必然自取灭亡。

equivalents: he who lives by the sword dies by the sword
give them enough rope and they'll hang themselves

examples.zh: 多行不义必自毙，这个贪官终于落网了。
examples.en: Evildoers destroy themselves — the corrupt official has finally been caught.

examples.zh: 他坏事做尽，多行不义必自毙。
examples.en: He's done every kind of wrong; he'll bring about his own downfall.

story.en: When ministers urged Duke Zhuang of Zheng to act against his ambitious brother Gongshu Duan, he replied: "Do much evil and you will surely destroy yourself. Just wait." (多行不义必自毙，子姑待之).
story.zh: 郑庄公对臣下说："多行不义必自毙，子姑待之。"后其弟共叔段果然叛乱失败。

natural: The hen flies off and the eggs break

meaning.en: To lose everything; end up with nothing.
meaning.zh: 鸡飞走了，蛋也打破了。比喻两头落空，一无所得。

examples.zh: 他想两边都占便宜，结果鸡飞蛋打。
examples.en: He tried to have it both ways and ended up with nothing.

examples.zh: 投资失败，他鸡飞蛋打，血本无归。
examples.en: The investment failed and he lost everything.

meaning.en: Successfully completed; mission accomplished.
meaning.zh: 原为佛教用语，指诵经等佛事结束。后比喻事情圆满结束。

examples.zh: 项目顺利完成，功德圆满。
examples.en: The project was completed successfully — mission accomplished.

examples.zh: 孩子们都成家立业了，老人觉得功德圆满。
examples.en: With the children all settled, the old couple feel their job is done.

usage.zh: 多作谓语，原为佛教用语。

meaning.en: Magnanimous; generous and forgiving.
meaning.zh: 形容度量大，能容人。

examples.zh: 他宽宏大量，原谅了伤害过他的人。
examples.en: Magnanimous, he forgave those who had hurt him.

examples.zh: 请您宽宏大量，原谅孩子的无礼。
examples.en: Please be big-hearted and forgive the child's rudeness.

natural: A bow's reflection in a cup mistaken for a snake

meaning.en: To be alarmed by imaginary fears.
meaning.zh: 把映在酒杯里的弓影当成蛇。比喻因疑神疑鬼而引起恐惧。

examples.zh: 他受过一次骗，现在杯弓蛇影，谁都不信。
examples.en: Having been scammed once, he jumps at shadows and trusts no one.

examples.zh: 别杯弓蛇影，那只是风声。
examples.en: Don't be paranoid — it's just the wind.

origin.source: 汉·应劭《风俗通义·怪神》；《晋书·乐广传》

story.en: A guest drank wine and saw a snake in his cup; he fell ill with fear. The host later showed him it was only the reflection of a bow hanging on the wall — and he recovered at once.
story.zh: 有人饮酒时看到杯中有蛇，回去后惊恐成病。后来主人告诉他那是墙上挂的弓的影子，病立刻好了。
